title: Would this be too laborious for you if you liked war games?
author: No_Departure7494
selftext:
Building a game now using a lot of real world data. It started as an experiment but then I realized I had become addicted to my own game, haha.

Picture naval combat but the mechanics and what not were kind of primitive. "10 cruise missiles left", or big battleship guns.

Now imagine you run out of cruise missiles and you need to replenish as an auxiliary ship. It can take 5-10 minutes round trip so you must use your munitions in an intelligent, strategic manner.

Would this bore you if it's not completely over the top?

comments.author: Novaworld7
comments.body: Build the best game you can build. Players will join. If you don't build what you love, you'll burn out.

replies.author: Briskfall
replies.body:
This. 👆

I'm just YOLOing at this point in a IDGAF if nobody will like it. If I can't even enjoy the process, then it's going to be torturous. (Though I know that it'll probably have no audience, haha!)

replies.author: 1relytnotyals
replies.body: Same bro! I’m making games I will enjoy . Although it is different from design and just being able to enjoy. I still am liking it

replies.author: egonosz
replies.body: You can build game which will be enjoyable by you and by players too. That not means that the first design you come up with is good. In this exact case OP will be able to play his game optimally from start so for him this will not look like punishment, but the new players who did not design the game for them this can feel as punishment. They may feel the OP made this in this way to elongate the play time. I am sure there are 1000 more ideas where this came from and all of which OP would enjoy it in same way or even more.

comments.author: No_Entrepreneur6548
comments.body: It depends on the context of what you’re doing with that time. In my game about an entire battle campaign there are auxiliaries. The ships have limited ammo and fuel. You can, if you want, fly supply missions. Or you can let things play out and ignore the logistics side. I think with ai tools it’s easier than ever to create a deeper logistics sim. But you should always allow players to play around it or fast sim though it. I think it’s awesome to see more wargames since they’ve been so hard to make save balance. Try to start with a rudimentary top down 3d browser game and expand from that if it feels right.

comments.author: Flashy-Whereas-3234
comments.body:
I would play that if it had a suitable "fast forward" time compression ability, so you can fast-forward through the times that are purely logistics operations.

Bonus points if fast forward disengages if something interesting happens, like being fired upon.

You could have a toggleable hardcore option which disables the speed skip, and that would likely be the best way for multiplayer to work (unless you have coop fast forwar).

Chances are, I won't fast forward if there's a battle, but I'm not sitting around for 10 minutes playing logistics simulator, I'll get distracted and then forget and die.  And that's not fun.

comments.author: Almaravarion
comments.body:
Let me put it this way - I LOVE Aurora4X. Fuel needs transport, ammunition and missiles need transporting, desgning and production, then transported to destination ship. Missile can be placed on a figher, which itself is in hangar of a carrier, each of which is composed of different components, each of which had to be researched and produced. Materials for maintenance has to be carried.

  
Make the best thing You can, You WILL find audience, just make sure it's high quality, rather than first-looks-only 'fine' product. Test it, then test it again, pay attention to performance; Little things but all of them can turn good product into junk. And for love of all that You deem Holy - dev this thing, and not vibe it few prompts to get minimum technically-fitting-description product, as many do.

comments.author: PositiveScarcity8909
comments.body: Yes, you are describing a small game mechanic, not a gameplay loop.
